input.quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.
input.rationale: The only liability limitation in the Agreement (p0077, inside the indemnity section) is one-sided: it caps TrueLink's liability at 12 months' hosting and support compensation while Client's liability — including the very broad indemnity in Section 12(a) — remains unlimited. That is walk-away territory under the rule (Customer uncapped while Vendor is capped), so the clause fails the fallback. The cap is also confined to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 and carves out only TrueLink's gross negligence and wilful misconduct, with no carve-out for indemnification or confidentiality breaches (Section 10). We target the fallback: the smallest edit makes the existing 12-month fee cap mutual and places indemnification obligations, breach of confidentiality obligations, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap, leaving the fee basis and the rest of the sentence verbatim. We have not pressed the preferred USD 1,000,000 floor, mutual consequential-damages exclusion or payment-obligation carve-out, which remain available if the parties reopen this clause.

proposal.summary: Make the 12-month fee cap mutual and place indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside it.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is a mutual cap of 12 months' fees with indemnification, confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct sitting outside the cap; as drafted the cap protects only TrueLink and leaves Client's liability unlimited. We have made the existing cap apply to both parties and carved those obligations out, leaving the fee basis untouched.
